title: Three-Tier Token Architecture (Global, Semantic, Component)
problemStatement:
Architecting a scalable design token hierarchy separating raw values (primitives) from intent (semantic alias) and component scoped tokens.

**Enterprise Importance**:
Without a 3-tier system, theming, dark mode, and multi-brand support break down into chaotic find-and-replace disasters across thousands of components.
interviewTrap: Exposing global tokens directly to component authors (e.g., `color: var(--blue-500)` instead of `color: var(--color-interactive-primary)`), which prevents dark mode or brand rebranding without rewriting component CSS.

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Tokens follow a strict unidirectional dependency graph: Component Tokens reference Semantic Tokens, which reference Global Primitive Tokens, which hold raw literal values (hex, rem, ms). Never allow components to reference global tokens directly.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Design Token Layer: Primitives, semantic aliases, and component tokens established.
2. Component Architecture: Headless state and keyboard accessibility hooks implemented.
3. Styling & Cascade: Zero-runtime CSS variables and layer specificity managed.
4. Governance & Packaging: Tree-shaking, semantic versioning, and telemetry monitored.

complexity.time: O(1) CSS variable resolution at paint time / zero JavaScript runtime overhead
complexity.space: O(1) bundle footprint per imported component
